description: HIAD, the Hydrogen Incidents and Accidents Database, is a repository of hydrogen-related unwanted events maintained by the European Commission's Joint Research Centre at Petten with financial support from the Clean Hydrogen Joint Undertaking and knowledge support from the European Hydrogen Safety Panel. Events come from primary or secondary sources such as news, inspection reports of public institutions, other public databases and scientific articles, each with a traceable link to the original source where possible, and JRC experts review and validate them before entry. Version 2.2 contains events up to 31 December 2025 and has been available since 16 March 2026, with a document explaining what is new and usage guidelines. Coverage is worldwide. Access: an Excel file and a beta interactive dashboard on the MINERVA page. Licence and cost: use is free of charge on acknowledgement of the JRC source, and the download implies acceptance of a no-liability notice. Caveats: quality depends on the original sources, the data are not meant to judge companies or countries, and without benchmarks the database cannot compare hydrogen with other technologies. It suits hydrogen risk and consequence modelling, safety training and resilience planning, and relates to the European Hydrogen Backbone map catalogued here.
